correctness.rationale: Every Gram entry is a normalized Ramanujan sum. At q consecutive columns no nonzero difference is divisible by q, giving three exact entry types. The rank-p class-sum correction to a scalar matrix has one top equality direction, s-1 large-class contrast modes, p-s-1 small-class contrasts, and a two-by-two quotient whose second eigenvalue is determined by trace. The formulas are valid including p=2 and s=1, with a single alternating-sign kernel for p=2 and the asserted exact sharp eigenvalues otherwise. Direct numerical construction and independent arithmetic Gram evaluation passed 465 assertions across 93 prime pairs; finite tests are auxiliary.

value.rationale: Primitive frequencies are a canonical arithmetic partial Fourier sampling set. The largest-prime-length consecutive block is the first natural maximal block before q-divisible differences enter its Gram, and q unknown coefficients against all phi(pq) primitive measurements is a concrete recovery problem. The complete four-level spectrum quantifies an exact odd-prime uniform stability law and a one-mode even-prime failure, gives sharp finite-frame bounds and arithmetic equality cases, and is not merely a renaming of a known full-circulant spectrum.
